data.title: The goddess Lada at Lietava Castle – a Slavic legend
data.excerpt: Long before the castle was founded, a pagan tribe of Slavs lived at the foot of the hill and built a sanctuary called a bosnica on its summit. In the legend a chariot of pure gold drawn by doves and swans stood in the middle of it, carrying the goddess Lada, from whose name Lietava is said to derive.
data.metaTitle: The goddess Lada at Lietava Castle
data.metaDescription: A legend of the pagan sanctuary on the hill of Lietava and of the goddess Lada, with her golden chariot drawn by doves and swans, long before the castle was built.

children.text: Long before the castle was founded, a pagan tribe of Slavs lived at the foot of the hill and built on its summit a sanctuary called a bosnica. The sanctuary was adorned with wooden figurines of Slavic gods, carved and painted.

In the middle of the sanctuary stood a chariot of pure gold, to which two snow-white doves and two swans were harnessed. In that chariot stood the enchanting, naked woman Lada; her rich, golden hair reached down to her knees, and upon it she wore a fine white crown for the hair, edged with a wreath of roses and myrtle. From her heart glowing fiery rays of ardent love shot out. In her right hand she held three apples, in her left a diamond globe. Behind her stood four maidenly figures, the so-called milostky, the maidens of love – Lada, Dzeva, Siva and the Fair Lady – passing an apple one to another. On the bank of the brook flowing near the sanctuary dwelt the priestesses of the deities, who in the hottest part of summer offered the goddesses a drink of mead, ripe ears of wheat and rye and fragrant wreaths of flowers. The rites were accompanied by the songs of maidens and of women in love. The priestesses would then reward them with charms against lovers who were growing cold. On the site of this pagan sanctuary, at the time when Christianity was spreading, a Christian church in the Gothic style was built, and later the castle that we know today under the name of Lietava. The name Lietava is derived from the name of the goddess Lada.
